title: Design Engineer
content_text:
About BMD
BMD is Australia’s leading integrated engineering, construction and urban development business, with foundations built on the family values that underpin our unique, collaborative approach. Driven by a purpose of powering futures and creating enduring legacies through a commitment to collaboration, BMD is delivering infrastructure solutions that connect and transform communities. With a proud history beginning in 1979, BMD now employs 2,400 people throughout Australia, the Philippines and United Kingdom.
About the Role
With a strong pipeline of major infrastructure projects across transport, water and renewable energy, we're seeking an experienced Design Engineer to join our growing NSW team. Working alongside our Design Manager and delivery team, you'll play a key role in managing the interface between design and construction, ensuring innovative, cost-effective and buildable solutions are delivered across complex Design & Construct projects. This is an opportunity to influence project outcomes from planning through to delivery while contributing to some of the state's most significant infrastructure projects.
You will:
- Coordinating and managing design delivery from external consultants and multidisciplinary design teams
- Supporting project teams throughout project development, tendering and delivery phases
- Driving collaboration between construction teams, clients, designers and key stakeholders
- Identifying and managing design risks, opportunities and value engineering initiatives
- Managing RFIs, technical queries, design changes and variation processes
- Facilitating design workshops, coordination meetings and stakeholder engagement activities
- Providing technical input into constructability reviews, methodologies and project planning
- Supporting tenders, bids and project pursuits across the NSW business
- Contributing to continuous improvement and design management best practice initiatives
About the Role
You bring experience delivering major civil infrastructure projects within Australia and have a passion for finding practical engineering solutions that support successful project outcomes. You'll ideally have experience across one or more of the following sectors:
- Transport infrastructure projects for Transport for NSW
- Water infrastructure projects for Sydney Water
- Renewable energy or wind farm developments
You will also possess:
- A degree qualification in Civil Engineering or a related discipline
- Experience working within Design & Construct project environments
- Strong capability managing design consultants and coordinating multidisciplinary teams
- Excellent stakeholder engagement, communication and relationship-building skills
- Well-developed commercial acumen and risk management capability
- The ability to drive innovation and continuously improve project outcomes
- Experience working on complex infrastructure projects within fast-paced delivery environments
Diversity and inclusion
We recognise that we are strengthened by diversity, and we embrace differences as an equal opportunity employer providing a flexible and inclusive workplace.
So, join our team, be yourself and help us power futures and create legacies.
We’re a purpose and values-led business guided by our values of family, empowered, collaborative and driven. For further details on what makes BMD unique, head to https://www.bmdgroup.global/careers
bullets: National contractor with a local feel - you're more than just a number at BMD
Shape design outcomes on complex Design & Construct projects
Contribute to landmark infrastructure project in Sydney's Western Suburbs

content_text:
SX5 is currently seeking a Project Engineer for a transportable building project (manufacture and installation) in the Pilbara . This role is Perth based during the manufacturing phase with the opportunity to go FIFO after 6 months.
The successful applicant must have strong technical abilities and be able to read and interpret drawings and specs. Have relevant experience in earthworks and installation of transportable buildings. Safety is a top priority for both SX5 and the client and we need someone who is safety-focused. The ability to communicate effectively and engage with the client is also crucial for this role
The onsite team will consist of approximately 20 personnel, supported by additional on and off site administration and project support. 
Essential Criteria:
- Engineering Qualification (Structural desired)
- At least 2 years experience - Project Engineer
- Experience in earthworks and Installation of transportable buildings
- Commitment to safe work practices
- Australian Drivers License
- Applicants must have full Australian working rights
Desirable Criteria:
- Rio Tinto Site Ready
Salary will be determined based on experience

content_text:
Our client provides Innovative and practical storage and racking solutions to customers across Australia. They work closely with various Stakeholders, sales teams, manufacturers and project partners to deliver solutions that are safe, compliant, cost-effective and tailored to each project.
They are seeking a Junior Designer / Estimator to join their team. This role will suit someone with experience in racking design and estimating, or a Graduate/Student Structural Engineer looking to develop their career in the industry.
About the Role
Working closely with their National Design Manager, you will help develop practical and cost-effective racking and storage solutions for our customers.
Your responsibilities will include:
- Reviewing customer requirements and project information.
- Preparing racking layouts and designs.
- Preparing material take-offs and bills of materials.
- Preparing project estimates and quotations.
- Obtaining supplier and subcontractor pricing.
- Supporting the Sales team with technical and estimating information.
- Coordinating information with suppliers, engineering, installation and other project teams.
- Ensuring designs and documentation are accurate and professional.
- Identifying tender opportunities through platforms such as EstimateOne.
- Maintaining project drawings and documentation.
- Providing general administration support to the Sales team when required.
About You
They are looking for someone who:
- Has experience in racking design and/or estimating, preferably.
- Has experience using AutoCAD or similar design software [key essential].
- Has experience with Cin7 [advantageous but not essential].
- Has strong attention to detail and accuracy.
- Has an interest or background in structural engineering, design or construction.
- Has good communication and organisational skills.
- Can work independently and as part of a team.
- Is reliable, professional and willing to learn.
The Opportunity
This is a great opportunity to join a growing business and develop your skills across design, estimating and project support within the racking and storage industry.
If you are motivated, detail-oriented and looking to develop your career, we would love to hear from you. Please forward your resume to recruitment@gteaustralia.com

title: Project Engineer - FIFO
content_text:
- FIFO Civil Engineer – 2:1 Roster 
 - Remote infrastructure projects, working with regional councils & DTMR
 - Queensland-owned civil contractor actively expanding its footprint across the region
Opportunity with a privately Queensland owned civil construction company who work within resources, local authorities and main road projects across QLD and remote areas. They deliver small to medium infrastructure projects such as roads, bridges & structures, drainage and remote civil works. This is a business with an emphasis on providing a long-term career opportunity. Led by a team of highly experienced professionals, the company ensures personal growth and hands-on site-based experience.
Due to project wins and company growth, this contractor is seeking a FIFO Project Engineer delivering projects ranging between $2M - $10M. You will work closely with the PM and Supervisor, planning the works, managing the crews, liaising with the client, ensuring the program is met, costings are accurate and quality assurance is recorded - exposure and responsibilities towards project management. To be successful you must have a minimum of 4 years delivering civil infrastructure, main roads or alike for a civil contractor in similar conditions.
Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
 - Planning, programming & resourcing
 - Procurement of key subcontractors and suppliers
 - Subcontractor management 
 - Monitoring Quality Assurance 
 - Liaising with clients, contractors & consultants 
 - Tracking and updating project program against contract baseline
 - Progress claims & variations
 - Reporting on a weekly & monthly basis
 - Ensuring Safety and Environmental standards are met
The successful Engineer must have at least 4 years of main roads - TMR, Council or similar civil infrastructure experience with relevant engineering qualifications. A steady work history going up through the ranks, on site delivering projects that consist of bulk earthworks, roads, structures to the specifications set by governing bodies.
This role will suit a hard-working professional who enjoys FIFO on 2:1 roster, working for a smaller-tier organisation, with a close-knit team where you will be valued and taken care of. This individual can be based anywhere in QLD and happy to travel! 
If you are feeling lost in a larger organisation, not being valued and compensated for your work, or just ready for a change to mix things up with a smaller, progressive contractor, apply now to find out further information!

title: Undergraduate Engineer
content_text:
Serco is a place where you can grow
Join a team of professionals across Asia Pacific and experience a place of challenge, opportunity and reward.
We offer benefits designed to support you as you develop your engineering career, including:
- Flexible work arrangements supporting a real work-life balance
- Ongoing professional development and training support
- Access to employee wellbeing and assistance programs
- Career opportunities within a multinational services company
- Employee Networks supporting diversity and inclusion
- Meaningful work supporting Australia's maritime capability
Make an Impact
If you're studying engineering or naval architecture and want to start applying what you're learning to a real maritime environment, this is an opportunity to build practical experience while completing your degree.
As an Undergraduate Engineer supporting the RSV Nuyina, you'll work alongside experienced engineers, technical specialists and project teams while developing your understanding of professional engineering delivery. You'll gain practical exposure to engineering standards, safety, risk, design and compliance while building the technical skills and judgement that will support your future career.
You'll also have access to engineering mentors who can help turn university theory into practical understanding and give you exposure to how complex maritime engineering work is managed and delivered.
You'll have the opportunity to:
- Support engineers with practical engineering and technical activities
- Contribute to engineering service delivery and on-site technical support
- Apply engineering standards, processes and compliance requirements
- Develop your maritime engineering knowledge and professional judgement
- Work alongside engineers, mentors and multidisciplinary project teams
- Build your understanding of safety, risk, design and project management
- Manage assigned work while delivering accurate and timely technical outputs
- Learn from experienced technical specialists and engineering professionals
Serco is a place for you
You'll be studying engineering or naval architecture and ready to gain practical experience in a maritime environment. You'll bring curiosity, initiative and a willingness to learn from experienced engineers and technical specialists, with university projects, placements or practical engineering experience highly regarded. Most importantly, you'll be motivated to develop your technical capability and build a career in engineering.
You'll need:
- Current enrolment at a recognised Australian university in an Engineering or Naval Architecture degree
- Developing technical knowledge and sound engineering judgement
- Strong communication skills and the ability to work with engineers, mentors and project teams
- An organised approach to balancing university and professional priorities
- A commitment to safety, environmental compliance and professional development
- The ability to obtain and maintain a minimum Baseline Australian Defence Security Clearance
Please note:
• This position carries trust and responsibility. To support this, a comprehensive probity assessment, including a National Police Check, is a key part of the selection process for this role.
• As this role requires an Australian Defence Security Clearance, applicants must be Australian Citizens and eligible to obtain and maintain that clearance. If successful, Serco will manage and sponsor the clearance process.
Are you ready to do important work that really matters?
At Serco, we bring together the right people, the right technology, and the right partners to create impactful solutions that address some of the world's most urgent and complex challenges.
We focus on serving governments all over the globe. The work we do has touched the lives of millions in Australia and New Zealand and offers unique opportunities to leverage your skills across our core capabilities in health, defence, maritime, justice, immigration, and community services.
We seek and celebrate diversity and encourage applications from all backgrounds and cultures including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, LGBTQI+, veterans and people with disability.
By joining Serco you'll have access to Employee Networks led by colleagues who are passionate about diversity, inclusion and belonging.
Impact a better future at Serco.

title: BIM Engineer
content_text:
Gamuda Australia is seeking an experienced BIM Engineer to join the project team delivering the Parramatta Integrated Station Development (ISD) in Sydney.
This is an exciting opportunity to work on a major multidisciplinary project incorporating significant building, services, infrastructure and station interfaces.
Working closely with the BIM, Digital Engineering, Design, Engineering and Construction teams, you will play an important role in ensuring BIM and digital engineering processes are effectively implemented and support the successful delivery of the project.
About the Role
As a BIM Engineer, you will support the implementation and coordination of BIM and digital engineering processes across the project. You will work with designers, consultants, engineers, subcontractors and construction teams to develop, coordinate and maintain accurate digital models and project information.
Key responsibilities will include:
- Support the implementation of BIM and digital engineering processes across the Parramatta ISD project.
- Develop, coordinate and maintain BIM models across multiple disciplines.
- Coordinate architectural, structural, civil, MEP and specialist services models.
- Undertake model reviews, clash detection and design coordination.
- Identify and assist in resolving design, coordination and constructability issues.
- Work closely with Design Managers, Engineers, Services teams and Construction Managers.
- Assist with BIM Execution Plans, project BIM standards and digital engineering requirements.
- Manage BIM deliverables and model information in accordance with project requirements.
- Support model federation and multidisciplinary coordination.
- Assist with model audits, quality assurance and information validation.
- Ensure BIM models and project information comply with relevant project standards and requirements.
- Support consultants, designers and subcontractors with BIM requirements and coordination.
- Assist with the management of Common Data Environments (CDEs) and digital collaboration platforms.
- Support the integration of BIM with construction planning, procurement, fabrication and installation.
- Identify opportunities to improve project delivery through digital engineering, technology and automation.
- Provide technical BIM and digital engineering support to project teams.
- Assist with the development and implementation of BIM workflows and processes.
About You
We are looking for a BIM professional with experience working on large-scale building, infrastructure or multidisciplinary construction projects.
You will ideally have:
- A degree, diploma or relevant qualification in Engineering, Construction, Architecture, Building Services, Digital Engineering or a related discipline.
- Experience working in a BIM, Digital Engineering or design coordination role within a construction or engineering environment.
- Experience working with multidisciplinary BIM models.
- Strong understanding of BIM methodologies, model coordination and information management.
- Experience coordinating architectural, structural, civil and MEP models.
- Experience with clash detection, model reviews and design coordination.
- Understanding of construction processes and design/constructability interfaces.
- Experience working with BIM Execution Plans, project BIM standards and digital engineering requirements.
- Strong understanding of Common Data Environments and digital collaboration platforms.
- Strong communication and coordination skills, with the ability to work effectively with designers, engineers, consultants and construction teams.
- Experience with BIM software such as Revit, Navisworks, Civil 3D, AutoCAD or similar platforms would be highly regarded.
Why Join Gamuda?
This is an opportunity to join a major international engineering and construction organisation and contribute to the delivery of a landmark project in Sydney.
You will gain exposure to complex building, station, services and infrastructure interfaces, while working alongside experienced BIM and Digital Engineering professionals.
You will also be part of a growing project environment, with opportunities to contribute to future major infrastructure and building projects across Australia.

Be part of a supportive team culture with a focus on delivery excellence
Grow your career with Gamuda Engineering Australia.

title: Engineer: Technical Solutions
screening_questions: Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
What's your expected annual base salary?
How much notice are you required to give your current employer?
Have you worked in a role which requires a sound understanding of as/NZ 5369 Standards?
How many years experience in Mining Exploration do you have?
content_text:
About Sarens
Sarens is a global leader in crane rental, heavy lifting, and engineered transport. Our work sits behind some of the biggest projects in mining, energy, wind, infrastructure, and construction. Our philosophy is simple: nothing too heavy, nothing too high. In Oceania, we support projects across Australia, Papua New Guinea, and New Caledonia from our bases in Maddington, WA and Hendra, QLD.
About the role
Reporting to the Technical Solutions and Engineering Manager, you'll turn complex lifting and transport challenges into safe, practical, and buildable plans. You'll work closely with our operations crews, project teams, and clients, and you'll see your engineering carried out on site.
What you'll do
- Prepare lift and rigging engineering, including lift plans, rigging designs, and crane selection
- Engineer transport routes for oversize and heavy loads
- Carry out structural design and checks for heavy lift works, including lifting beams, frames, and temporary works
- Assess ground conditions and bearing capacity for crane and transport setups
- Design custom solutions where standard equipment won't do the job
- Produce calculations, drawings, and method statements that crews can follow on site
- Support tenders and project planning with technical input
- Visit sites to review conditions and support critical lifts
What you'll bring
- A degree in Civil, Structural, or Mechanical Engineering
- 3+ years' experience in heavy lift, cranage, rigging, transport, or temporary works engineering
- Working knowledge of relevant Australian Standards, such as AS 2550 and AS 4100
- Experience with lift planning, CAD, and structural analysis software
- A practical mindset: you want your designs to work on the ground, not just on paper
- Clear communication with crews, supervisors, and clients alike
- A strong commitment to safety
- Full Australian working rights and a current driver's licence
Desirable
- Chartered status (CPEng) or working towards it
- Experience in wind, mining, or energy projects
What we offer
- Competitive salary plus superannuation
- Technical support and knowledge sharing from Sarens engineers worldwide
- A varied workload where no two projects are the same
Ready to apply?
Click Apply and send us your resume and a short cover letter telling us about a lift or engineering challenge you're proud of. Only candidates with full Australian working rights will be considered.

Work on Major infrastructure Projects

title: Graduate Project Officer
content_text:
Design the future of a growing city
Our Project Management and Design teams turn vision into reality, delivering the infrastructure and public spaces that shape how people live, move and connect. This is work with scale and impact, supported by a collaborative culture, professional growth opportunities and the stability to build both your career and your legacy.
As a Graduate Project Officer, you help deliver Council’s Western Sydney Infrastructure Grant Program and other transformational projects that support the growth of Blacktown City. You work closely with project managers, consultants, contractors and Council teams to coordinate projects from planning through to delivery. Your work includes preparing project plans and budgets, managing tender and RFQ processes, supporting contract administration, maintaining project registers and records, and preparing reports, briefs and correspondence for Council and senior stakeholders.
You monitor project progress, identify risks, resolve issues and help keep projects on track, within budget and aligned with project objectives. You contribute to audits, business cases, capital works reviews and governance requirements while building strong relationships across Council and with external partners. Every project you support helps deliver infrastructure, facilities and workplace improvements that benefit employees and the community.
At Blacktown City, every project has a purpose. Our varied project portfolio gives you the opportunity to build practical project management skills, learn from experienced professionals and gain exposure to complex projects that leave a lasting impact across the city. Flexible working arrangements, a supportive team environment and the stability of local government provide the foundation for a rewarding career.
This role suits a motivated graduate with qualifications in construction project management, engineering or a related field. If you enjoy solving problems, working with different stakeholders, managing competing priorities and seeing projects progress from concept to completion, you will thrive in this role.
At Blacktown City Council, good people make great teams, and great teams build great cities. Here, you will find the stability and support to keep growing, along with:
 - a term contract, full-time role for up to 2 years and 9 months with one of Australia's largest councils 
 - an entry level salary commencing at $1,866.69 per week
 - a 35-hour working week 
 - access to Council's flextime arrangement
 - 12% superannuation and competitive leave entitlements
 - ongoing training and development support
 - access to Fitness Passport, social clubs and wellbeing programs.
 Our commitment to safety
Blacktown City Council is committed to safety. We have introduced alcohol and other drug testing at the pre-employment phase, and via a series of random and cause testing.
We are a child safe organisation that supports and promotes the safety, wellbeing and empowerment of children.
Position description
For more detail on this opportunity, click here to view or download the position description. 
Closing date: Sunday 18 October 2026, 11.59 pm 
Contact officer: Tam Nahar on 9839 5918
Internal ref: Term contract - 2 years and 9 months

title: Engineer - Water and Wastewater Design
location: Tweed Heads, Lismore & Far North Coast NSW
content_text:
Work alongside experienced engineering professionals to support the planning, construction and management of vital community infrastructure projects, spanning roads, water, sewer, drainage and flood management.
 In this role, you will provide support to Senior Engineers, Coordinators and Managers in a diverse range of Planning, Policy, Design, Construction, Contact Management, Project Management, and Operations areas relating to water supply and sewerage services.
 The Engineer - Water and Wastewater Design is a professional position with experience and knowledge in the fields of hydraulic, water supply and sewerage conveyancing.
 About the role:
 - Work across a variety of units and sections within the Engineering Division, gaining broad exposure to local government engineering functions.
 - Participate in rotational opportunities across the Division, providing valuable experience and supporting career development within Council.
 - Demonstrate a willingness to learn, adapt and contribute in a range of work environments and engineering disciplines.
 - Build strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills through regular interaction with consultants, contractors, Councillors, staff and community members.
 - Take part in ongoing performance, training and development activities, with opportunities to undertake higher duties as required.
 What's on offer:
 - a base salary ranging from $102,118 per annum with competency-based increments up to $117,528 per annum, plus 12% super
 - 70-hour, 9 day fortnight
 - training and development opportunities
 - flexible work options for a healthy work/life balance
 - generous employment conditions (we have too many to list - click here for more).
 We are seeking:
 - A qualified Civil Engineer with a Bachelor of Civil Engineering (or a related discipline) and eligibility for membership of Engineers Australia, or equivalent technical experience and expertise.
 - Experience supporting the design and delivery of engineering infrastructure projects.
 - Knowledge of water supply and sewerage infrastructure, including planning, design and construction principles.
 - A genuine interest in developing skills across a diverse range of local government engineering functions.
 - Well-developed communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build effective working relationships with a range of stakeholders.
 About us:
 - Located on the picturesque far North Coast of NSW, bordering the Gold Coast.
 - The Tweed is a vibrant, diverse location offering a lifestyle near the water, in a rainforest or on a farm. 
 - Tweed Shire Council is committed to employment equity and diversity and encourages applications from people of all ages, abilities and backgrounds in both traditional and non-traditional roles. We provide workplace adjustments for people with disability, and access to flexible work options. 
 - Join an employer of choice. Professionals Australia (Local Government Engineers’ Association) has named Council the 2021 and 2025 Employer of Choice for our great employment practices within NSW local government. 
 Where it's located:
 This position is based in Tweed Heads and can be directed to work from any Council work site.
 Position closes: 
 Friday 16 October 2026 at 12 noon sharp (NSW time). Late applications will not be permitted.

title: Project Engineer
content_text:
We are seeking an Asphalt Project Engineer to join our team and focus of the delivery of the North East Link Project, Victoria's largest transport infrastructure project.
At Downer we plan, create and sustain. Downer is the leading provider of integrated services in Australia and New Zealand. Through trusted relationships and world leading insight we work closely with our customers to design, build and sustain assets, infrastructure, and facilities. 
Project Engineer
The Opportunity
We are seeking an Asphalt Project Engineer to join our team and focus of the delivery of the North East Link Project, Victoria's largest transport infrastructure project.
This is a fantastic opportunity to play a key role in the successful delivery of complex civil and asphalt construction works while working alongside some of the industry's most experienced professionals. You'll take ownership of project outcomes, drive performance across safety, quality, programme and cost.
What You'll Be Doing
As a Project Engineer, you'll be responsible for:
- Managing the delivery of allocated projects from planning through to completion
- Ensuring projects are delivered safely, on time, within budget and to specification
- Monitoring commercial performance, forecasting and cost control
- Managing subcontractors, suppliers and project stakeholders
- Driving project programmes and identifying opportunities to improve performance
- Leading risk management and ensuring timely resolution of project issues
- Preparing and reviewing project reports, claims and contractual documentation
- Supporting tender development and estimating activities
- Building and maintaining strong client relationships
- Championing Downer's Zero Harm culture and safety leadership expectations
What You'll Bring
- A degree qualification in Civil Engineering or a related discipline
- Proven experience delivering civil construction, asphalt, surfacing or infrastructure projects
- Strong commercial acumen with experience managing project budgets, forecasts and cost control
- Sound understanding of contract administration and project delivery methodologies
- Demonstrated ability to lead project outcomes in a collaborative environment
- Strong stakeholder management and communication skills
- A proactive approach to problem solving and continuous improvement
- A commitment to safety leadership and fostering a Zero Harm culture
Why Join Downer?
This is your opportunity to work on a career-defining infrastructure project while building your engineering capabilities within a supportive and experienced team.
In return, we offer:
- Exposure to one of Victoria's largest transport infrastructure projects
- Ongoing career development and internal progression opportunities
- A collaborative team culture that encourages innovation and learning
- Access to industry-leading systems, training and mentoring
- Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
- Health and wellbeing initiatives and discounts
- Perks@Downer employee benefits program
- A strong commitment to diversity, inclusion and flexible thinking
Ready to help deliver one of Victoria's most important infrastructure projects? Apply now and join the Downer team.
Reference Number: 736951
Apply now with your resume and a brief cover letter. For more information, contact Amy Isgar at TIrecruitmentAU@downergroup.com
At Downer, we value the diverse experiences, talents and cultures of our people and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive.

title: Project Engineer
content_text:
The City of Subiaco is going through a transformation with significant change and evolution in terms of residential options, the commercial sector, retail, entertainment, leisure and recreation. Navigating this change in partnership with the community, businesses and stakeholders, whilst also celebrating Subiaco’s heritage, history and culture is an exciting challenge. 
About the Role 
The City of Subiaco is recruiting a Project Engineer to join the Engineering Services branch on a permanent full-time basis. This role sits in the Engineering Services branch and will assist with the design and delivery of civil engineering projects and capital works.
The key responsibilities of this role include:
•    Assist the Principal Engineer with the design and delivery of engineering projects/capital works program.
•    Monitor and ensure all projects are completed on time, on budget and to the specified quality in accordance with the City's standard policies and procedures.
•    Ensure quality control is effectively managed including enforcement of non-conformance, if quality is not adhered.
•    Liaise and coordinate with internal and external customers during all phases of the projects. 
•    Manage site briefings to contractors for project scope.
•    Develop budgets and cost estimates.
•    Review contract documentation, specifications for infrastructure assets.
•    Preparation of tender documentation for infrastructure assets including liaising with WALGA to manage contracts.
•    Providing a high standard of customer service to the city’s residents to keep them abreast of project scope and timelines, including addressing their concerns during planning and execution stages. 
•    Assist the Principal Engineer and Senior Project Engineer with the preparation of MRRG funding submissions and other funding applications.
•    Prepare an annual report on the assessment of the condition of roads, footpaths, street lighting, including CCTV inspection reports for drainage infrastructure. 
•    Support the Asset Management team in updating the infrastructure inventory and condition ratings for various assets as required. 
•    Report year-to-date (YTD) expenditure on capital works projects as requested by the Principal Engineer for acquittal purposes. 
•    Attending capital works meetings and providing updates on projects to the team.
•    Any other duties as required.
Further information about this position can be found on the position description, found with this advertisement on the City's website.
Essential Requirements
•    Tertiary qualification in engineering or equivalent qualification with the eligibility for membership to the Institute of Engineers of Australia 
•    Extensive experience in Project Management in Local Government industry or in the similar field.
•    Demonstrated skills and experience in Contracts Management and Civil Engineering design. 
•    Demonstrated Skills and knowledge in preparing contract documentation, specifications and reviewing the existing tender documentation and specifications.
•    Highly developed skills in preparing estimates and budgetary measures.
•    Comprehensive skills and knowledge in Road construction industry including Drainage and Buildings and relevant statutory requirements.
•    Excellent leadership, team building and management skills
•    Advanced computer literacy skills and experience in the effective usage of project management module preferably Microsoft projects.
•    Ability to demonstrate a genuine commitment and responsiveness in providing the highest quality of customer service.
•    Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal.
•    Demonstrated conflict resolution skills.
•    Demonstrated experience in supervising and managing consultants/contractors.
•    Experience and knowledge of the Occupational Health and safety Act and standards relevant to Local Government Industry.
Desirable criteria:
•    Sound knowledge and understanding of WALGA contracts
•    Sound knowledge of Local Government legislation, principles and procedures.
Salary Package
In line with the City of Subiaco Inside Staff Industrial Agreement 2025, this position is classified as a Level 8. The salary range is $126,477.00 to $135,088.20 per annum, exclusive of superannuation. 
Working for the City of Subiaco
The City of Subiaco’s culture is community-focused, collaborative, inclusive and safety-oriented. On joining the team, you’ll receive great benefits, including training and development opportunities to expand your talents. Whether you’re located in an office or out in the field, everyone who works at the City reflects the values of Supportive, United, Bold and Impactful. 
Benefits to help you a achieve a positive work-life balance include, but are not limited to:
•    Up to 5 weeks annual leave plus the option to accrue time in lieu.
•    Sustainable travel allowance, or a parking permit.
•    Free membership to Lords Recreation Centre.
•    Superannuation co-contributions.
•    Up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave.
•    24/7 employee assistance programme.
•    Learning and development opportunities.
•    Novated lease and salary packaging options. 
See what other benefits the City can offer you on the City's website.
Enquiries about this role can be made to Randhir Karma – Manager Engineering Services  at randhirk@subiaco.wa.gov.au
For further assistance and queries regarding the application process, please contact our HR team at recruitment@subiaco.wa.gov.au
Application Process:
To apply for this position, please click apply and follow the prompts to submit your application. You will be asked to upload a CV and cover letter to support your application. 
To be considered for the role, it is essential that you demonstrate in your application how you meet the essential requirements. You should ensure that the information you provide in your application is relevant to the job role and is a true and accurate reflection of your experience and skill set. 
As an equal opportunity employer, people of diverse backgrounds, genders, cultures, differing abilities and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders are encouraged to apply. We recognise that we are strengthened by diversity and are committed to providing a diverse and inclusive work environment in which everyone is included and treated fairly with respect.
Closing Date:
Thursday 29 October 2026. The City of Subiaco reserves the right to commence shortlisting and interviews earlier than the commencement date. The City also reserves the right to close the vacancy early. If you are interested in this position, please submit an application as early as possible. 
Applicants must have the right to work in Australia.

content_text:
About Us
For more than 60 years, Complex Co. has been known for delivering award winning construction projects across the built environment.
Our skillful execution of quality projects is an expression of our personal and professional commitment to connecting and enhancing communities.
This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced Civil or Structural Engineer who wants to be part of an established and respected contractor with a strong future pipeline, a collaborative culture, and a reputation for excellence.
At Complex Co., we don't just construct buildings and infrastructure. We create places that support communities, businesses and future growth.
Our teams are delivering complex, technically challenging work across multiple sectors. From large-scale commercial developments through to critical civil infrastructure, we continue to build on a legacy of quality, safety and innovation that spans more than six decades.
Our success is built on our people. We invest in capable professionals who are passionate about construction, committed to continuous improvement, and driven to deliver exceptional outcomes for our clients and communities.
The Opportunity
As our commercial building pipeline continues to grow, we are seeking a Project Engineer to join our team and play a key role in delivering a diverse portfolio of high-quality commercial construction and civil infrastructure projects across the ACT and surrounding regions.
As our Project Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in planning, coordinating and delivering projects from commencement through to completion. You will work closely with project teams, subcontractors, consultants and clients to ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, on budget and to the highest quality standards
Key Responsibilities
- Lead the planning, coordination and delivery of civil construction projects
- Manage RFIs, design coordination, variations and change events
- Ensure construction activities comply with current drawings, specifications and standards
- Prepare and monitor project programs in consultation with Project Managers
- Oversee subcontractors, procurement, material tracking and project deliverables
- Manage project financials including forecasting, cost reporting and productivity tracking
- Prepare and assist with monthly progress claims, cash flow reporting and project forecasting
- Monitor WHS, QA and environmental compliance across projects
- Assist with internal audits, risk management and WHSEQA implementation
- Coordinate and prepare project documentation, reports and meeting minutes
- Mentor and support Site Engineers and junior project staff
- Maintain strong working relationships with clients, consultants, subcontractors and stakeholders
- Drive project outcomes while maintaining safety, quality and commercial performance standards
About You
We are seeking a motivated engineering professional who enjoys working in a fast paced project environment and takes in delivering exceptional outcomes. To be successful in this role, you will ideally have:
- A Bachelor's Degree in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering or a related discipline.
- Registration with Engineers Australia, CPEng and/ or eligibility to be Nationally Registered
- Experience delivering commercial building, structural or civil infrastructure projects.
- Strong technical, planning and problem-solving capabilities.
- Sound financial and contractual awareness.
- Excellent communication and relationship management skills.
- A commitment to safety, quality and continuous improvement.
Requirements
- Current Australian driver's licence
- Construction Industry White Card
- Asbestos Awareness Training
- Crystalline Silica Exposure Prevention Training
- Ability to obtain or hold relevant site-based certifications and inductions
- Engineers Australia registration or ACT Registered Engineer highly regarded
- Must have Australian work rights at the time of application
The Complex Co. Difference
When you join Complex Co., you'll become part of a team that:
- Delivers projects that genuinely impact and improve communities.
- Has a strong and growing pipeline of commercial and civil work.
- Values collaboration, accountability and high performance.
- Invests in professional development and career progression.
- Encourages innovation and practical problem-solving.
- Rewards and recognises the contribution of its people and celebrates success as a team
To Apply
If you are a Civil or Structural Engineer looking for an opportunity to join a team that has outstanding culture and contribute to award-winning projects we'd love to hear from you.
Click Apply Now or send your CV and a brief cover letter outlining your experience to:
hr@complexco.com.au

title: Graduate Engineer
content_text:
Permanent - Full Time
 Brisbane
 Are you a Graduate Engineer looking for more than just a desk-based graduate role?
Global Group is looking for a Brisbane-based Graduate Engineer to join our project team, supporting the estimating, planning and delivery of oil & gas construction projects.
This is an opportunity to build strong commercial and technical foundations at the front end of projects, while working closely with the people who deliver them in the field. As your experience grows, so will your exposure including opportunities to spend time on site and progress into Site Engineer and Project Engineer pathways.
 What you’ll be doing
Working alongside experienced project and construction professionals, you’ll gain hands-on exposure across the project lifecycle, including:
 - Preparing project estimates, durations and resource requirements
 - Assisting with project planning and construction schedules, including exposure to Primavera P6
 - Reviewing drawings, specifications and project documentation
 - Working with site teams to understand scope, constructability and execution requirements
 - Supporting tenders and front-end project activities
 - Building your understanding of pipelines, piping, facilities and oil & gas construction
 - Developing the skills to progress into site and project engineering opportunities
About you
We’re looking for someone at the beginning of their engineering career who is curious, driven and keen to learn.
You’ll ideally have:
 - A Bachelor’s degree in Civil or Mechanical Engineering
 - Graduate to approximately 1–2 years’ relevant experience
 - An interest in construction, projects and the oil & gas industry
 - Strong communication, problem-solving and organisational skills

 - Current Brisbane residency, this role is based in our Brisbane office.

Working alongside experienced project and construction professionals, you’ll gain hands-on exposure across the project lifecycle, including:
- Preparing project estimates, durations and resource requirements
- Working with site teams to understand scope, constructability and execution requirements
- A Bachelor’s degree in Civil or Mechanical Engineering
- Graduate to approximately 1–2 years’ relevant experience
- A current driver’s licence and Australian working rights
